A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 21 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, equations, figures and tables, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original synthetic SCM experiments and evaluations of the proposed methods on PetShop.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic experiments, runtime measurements and PetShop evaluations, including results under random tie resolution.

M1.justification: The three RCA methods remain, but Eq. 5 changes the empirical tail count from including the scored observation to excluding it. Algorithm 1 also rewrites TOCA's reverse randomization sweep as a forward conditioning sweep. These are limited revisions to the stated procedures; corresponding implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic linear/nonlinear SCMs and the same PetShop latency and availability tasks under low, high and temporal traffic. Additional graph sizes change experimental configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: PetShop gains a standard Traversal comparator alongside the retained dataset-specific baseline, renamed PetShop Traversal. TOCA disappears from the PetShop comparison. The synthetic experiments retain the same six methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds PetShop evaluations with random selection among highest-score ties, alongside explicitly tie-inclusive top-k reporting; v1 reports top-k recall without specifying tie handling. This materially expands the retrieval evaluation design. Runtime testing also extends from 50/100-node graphs to 1000 nodes.

E4.justification: New PetShop tie-resolution analyses in Tables 3–4 investigate whether high recall survives selecting among tied candidates, revealing roughly tenfold reductions in top-1 recall. This adds a substantial diagnostic of practical performance absent from v1. Runtime scalability analysis also extends to 1000-node graphs.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions per anomaly strength and display runtime distributions using boxplots. No new experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, seed disclosures or repeated-run counts are reported. Random tie resolution changes evaluation, without adding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: PetShop results are substantially revised and expanded. For low-traffic latency, SCORE ORDERING's top-1 recall is 0.29 in v1 Table 1; v2 reports 1.00 with ties and 0.10 with random tie resolution, which are not established same-setting gains. TOCA's PetShop results disappear, while anomaly-strength curves and 1000-node runtimes are newly displayed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Lemmas 4.3–4.5 on independent generation and bounds without pointwise monotonicity, plus Theorem 4.10 and its chain-recovery proof. Section 3 revises dominance conditions and adds a union-bound guarantee. Much existing TOCA mathematics is also reorganized, which alone would not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution of three simplified RCA methods remains. v2's introduction adds the explicit empirical claim that these simplifications do not heavily impair unique-root-cause identification; its abstract also foregrounds the probability-bound rationale.

C2.justification: v2 recommends TOCA only for rare cases with known conditional probabilities, explains PetShop score saturation and the usefulness of candidate shortlists, and discusses additional conditions for chain recovery. These substantially expand applicability guidance. Conversely, v1's explicit discussion of TOCA failing on PetShop is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the Apple M1 MacBook Pro with 16 GB memory, explains using reconstructed observed noises when their distributions are unknown, and specifies Matplotlib's default boxplot implementation. The detailed SCM generator, 1000 normal observations and 100 repetitions were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 connects anomaly-based discovery to distributional-change research through added Tian–Pearl and Zhang et al. citations. Matplotlib is added and the explicit DoWhy-GCM reference disappears. The separately cited RCA preprint is consolidated with the retained published work, rather than removed.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten around an oracle TOCA description; pseudocode, properties and sample complexity move into a dedicated appendix. The smooth-traversal subsection is merged into the multiple-node analysis, and experimental interpretation is reorganized and expanded. Contribution notation and explanatory prose are revised throughout.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1's duplicated graph-size plot with the intended anomaly-strength plot, combines runtime displays into a three-panel figure, and restyles Figure 3. PetShop reporting expands from two tables to four with revised columns and tie captions, while the algorithm box moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Figure 1 and makes PetShop's tie sensitivity substantially clearer, but removes TOCA's poor PetShop results. It also changes Eq. 5 so the tail count can be zero while retaining the claimed log-k upper bound; the new Theorem 4.10 and its proof use inconsistent scaling and epsilon terms. These reporting gains and unresolved technical regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
